title: Spiti Valley Bike Trip: Route, Season and Riding Tips

metaDescription: Plan a Spiti Valley bike trip: the Shimla to Kaza to Manali circuit, day-by-day distances, when Kunzum Pass opens, fuel, permits and road conditions.
description: A route guide to riding the Spiti Valley circuit by motorcycle: in from Shimla through Kinnaur, out over Kunzum Pass and the Atal Tunnel to Manali, with a day-by-day plan, the riding season, road conditions, fuel stops, permits for foreigners and altitude advice.
dek: The Spiti circuit is one of India's great rides: apple orchards, cliff roads, desert villages and a 4,551-metre pass. Here is how to plan it.

hero.alt: A road cut into sheer cliffs on the way to Spiti Valley
hero.caption: The road to Spiti

intro: Spiti is a high, dry valley in Lahaul and Spiti district of Himachal Pradesh, on the Tibetan side of the Himalaya. It can be reached from two directions: from Shimla along the Sutlej through Kinnaur, a road that stays open most of the year, or from Manali over Kunzum Pass, which is open only for a few months in summer.

Riding in from Shimla and out to Manali makes a loop of roughly 900 to 1,000 km. The Shimla side climbs gradually, which helps your body adjust to altitude, and the Kunzum side saves the roughest riding for the end, when you are acclimatised. This guide lays out the route, the season and what to prepare. For sights, stays and food in Spiti, see our Spiti Valley travel guide.
quickAnswer: The classic Spiti Valley bike trip is a loop of roughly 900 to 1,000 km: Shimla to Kaza through Kinnaur, then Kaza to Manali over Kunzum Pass (about 4,551 metres) and through the Atal Tunnel. Ride it in 8 to 10 days between about mid-June and early October, when Kunzum is open. Enter via Shimla to acclimatise, fill fuel at Kaza, and cross the streams near Chhatru in the morning.
takeaways: Ride in from Shimla through Kinnaur and out via Kunzum Pass to Manali for easier acclimatisation.
Kunzum Pass usually opens in June and closes around October or November, depending on snow.
The stretch from Losar over Kunzum to Gramphu is the roughest, with water crossings and broken road.
Kaza has a fuel station; carry extra fuel for the Kaza to Manali leg.
Foreign nationals need an Inner Line Permit for the Kinnaur border stretch; Indians do not.

sections.heading: The route, day by day
paras: Distances and times are approximate and depend on road works and weather. Add rest days in Kaza for side trips and acclimatisation.

rows: Shimla to Narkanda to Sarahan or Sangla
Apple country; Bhimakali temple at Sarahan, or detour to Sangla and Chitkul
Views of Kinner Kailash; foreigners get permits here
Cliff roads along the Sutlej; Nako lake village at about 3,600 m
Via the Malling nala; Tabo's thousand-year-old monastery
Dhankar monastery on a cliff; reach Kaza
Key monastery, Kibber, Langza, Komic, Hikkim, Pin Valley
Over Kunzum Pass; camp near Chandratal

sections.heading: When to ride
paras: The Shimla to Kaza road through Kinnaur is open most of the year, but snow and landslides can block it in winter and the monsoon. The Kaza to Manali road over Kunzum Pass is usually opened by the Border Roads Organisation in June and stays open until snow closes it, often in October or November.

Mid-June to September is the main riding season. July and August bring monsoon rain to Kinnaur and the Manali side, with landslide risk, though Spiti itself stays mostly dry. September is often the best month: clear skies, fewer tourists and rivers lower after the snowmelt.

items.name: Shimla to Kaza
body: Mostly paved, but with long landslide zones in Kinnaur, cliff sections and ongoing road works. Stretches around Malling and Nako are known for rockfall and slides.

items.name: Kaza to Losar
body: Good tarmac through the widening Spiti valley.

items.name: Losar to Gramphu over Kunzum
body: The hardest part: rocky, loose road over Kunzum Pass, dust or mud depending on weather, and several stream crossings between Batal and Chhatru. Some of these fill up with snowmelt in the afternoon, so ride this section early.

items.name: Chandratal detour
body: A narrow dirt track of about 14 km from near Batal to the lake parking area. Camps are set back from the lake; walk the last part.

sections.heading: Fuel, food, network and repairs
list: Fuel: stations at Reckong Peo and Kaza. There is none between Kaza and the Manali side, so carry extra fuel if your tank is small.
Food and stays: homestays and guesthouses in every main village; basic dhabas at Batal and Chhatru.
Mobile network: patchy. BSNL and some private networks work in Kaza and larger villages; do not rely on data. Download offline maps.
Repairs: small mechanics in Reckong Peo and Kaza. Carry spares and know basic repairs.
ATMs: in Reckong Peo and Kaza, but they can run out of cash. Carry enough cash.

sections.heading: Permits
paras: Indian citizens do not need a permit for Spiti. Foreign nationals need an Inner Line Permit for the stretch of Kinnaur near the Tibet border, roughly between Reckong Peo and Sumdo; it is issued in places such as Reckong Peo, Shimla and Kaza. Check current rules, and carry copies of your permit, licence and vehicle papers.

sections.heading: Which bike, rent or own?
paras: Any well-maintained bike of 350 cc or more with good ground clearance copes; many riders use Royal Enfield Himalayans or Classics, or similar adventure bikes. Rentals are available in Shimla and Manali. Check tyres, brakes and chain before leaving, and agree what happens if the bike breaks down in Spiti.

safety: Gain height gradually on Himalayan routes, sleep lower than your highest point where possible, and descend if altitude sickness symptoms (headache, nausea, breathlessness at rest) get worse.
Ride only in daylight; the Kinnaur cliff roads and Kunzum stretch are dangerous in the dark.
Walk stream crossings before riding them if unsure, and cross early in the day.
Watch for rockfall in Kinnaur, especially after rain.
Ride with at least one other bike; help can be hours away.
Carry warm and waterproof layers; weather at Kunzum changes fast.
Check the status of Kunzum Pass and the Kinnaur road with local police or the BRO before setting out.
packing: Riding jacket, trousers, gloves and boots
Puncture kit, spare tubes, cables and a tool kit
Cash, offline maps and a power bank

faqs.q: When is the best time for a Spiti Valley bike trip?
faqs.a: About mid-June to September, with September often the best month. Kunzum Pass opens around June and closes with snow in October or November.

faqs.q: Which route is better for Spiti, Shimla or Manali?
faqs.a: Enter from Shimla through Kinnaur for gradual acclimatisation, and exit over Kunzum Pass to Manali.

faqs.q: How many days are needed for a Spiti bike trip?
faqs.a: Eight to ten days for the full circuit, including a day or two around Kaza.

faqs.q: Is there a petrol pump in Spiti?
faqs.a: Yes, in Kaza. There is none between Kaza and the Manali side, so carry extra fuel.

faqs.q: Do I need a permit for Spiti?
faqs.a: Indians do not. Foreign nationals need an Inner Line Permit for the Kinnaur border stretch.
